article.title: Mimir

image.alt: Detailed screenshot of the Mimir platform
image.caption: Mimir is a dark and modern social media platform built for the JS2, CSS Frameworks & POR2 assignments.

sections.heading: Project overview
paragraph: Mimir is a responsive social media platform built for the JavaScript 2, CSS Frameworks, and Portfolio 2 assignments at NOROFF School of Technology and Digital Media. Users can create accounts, publish image-based posts, follow other users, search the feed, react to posts, and add comments.

The project began as a JavaScript application connected to the Noroff Social API. Its visual identity is inspired by the Mannaz rune, which represents people and human connection, making it a fitting foundation for a social platform. This is reflected in the dark interface, rune-inspired imagery, responsive layouts, and accessible interactions.

sections.heading: Development process
paragraph: The first stage was developed for the JavaScript 2 assignment, with the main focus on building the application logic and connecting the interface to the Noroff API. This included authentication, post CRUD functionality, profiles, following, searching, reactions, and comments.

For the CSS Frameworks assignment, I chose to continue improving Mimir rather than start a separate page. I migrated the interface to Tailwind CSS while keeping the existing visual identity and making the layouts more consistent across the application.

The final stage, Portfolio 2, focused on refinement. I used feedback from the earlier assignments to improve the presentation, remove unused code and files, strengthen error handling, fix broken interactions, improve form usability, and add details such as password visibility toggles and fallbacks for broken images.

sections.heading: Technology and Outcome
paragraph: The project uses JavaScript with ES6 modules, HTML, Tailwind CSS, and the Noroff Social API. It is deployed as a static site through Vercel.

Mimir demonstrates how a project can grow through several stages: first establishing reliable functionality, then improving the visual system, and finally refining the details that make the application feel complete and presentable.

image.caption: A Mimir post view with social interactions.

improvementReason: - Removed unused legacy CSS files and stale stylesheet imports.
- Removed console.error instances and personal, informal, and unnecessary comments.
- Updated the README to document the JS2, CSS Frameworks, and POR2 assignments.
- Added a reusable image fallback for broken image URLs.
- Fixed transparent cards and images by defining cardBackground and correcting stacking order.
- Fixed the comment modal background and broken send icon path.
- Added show/hide password toggles to login and registration forms.
- Matched register form field sizing with the login form.
- Fixed duplicate like counts when liking posts.
- Changed pagination text to white.
- Removed the unused Favorites navigation item because the API does not support saved favorites.
- Added the Mimir logo to the unauthenticated home-page message.
- Rebuilt and validated Tailwind CSS throughout the changes.
article.process: The project involved planning the interface, connecting the frontend to the API, building reusable UI patterns, and testing the main user flows.

article.title: Butta

image.alt: Image of the Butta landing page
image.caption: Butta was a quick project where I explored component-driven interfaces, structured frontend code, and practical problem solving in a JavaScript framework context.

sections.heading: Project overview
paragraph: Butta is a responsive e-commerce front-end built with React, TypeScript, and Vite. It fetches products from the Noroff Online Shop API and lets users browse products, search and sort items, view product details, manage a cart, and complete a mock checkout flow.

The project was originally created as a short introductory assignment for the JS Frameworks course, focused on learning the fundamentals of React, TypeScript, API integration, routing, and state management. It has since been refurbished for the POR2 assignment with visual, accessibility, performance, and maintainability improvements.

sections.heading: Development process
paragraph: Butta was created for the JavaScript Frameworks assignment at NOROFF. The goal was to build a functional, responsive online shop using React, TypeScript, and a REST API.

For Portfolio 2, the original project was refurbished for professional presentation. The work addressed feedback, accessibility, maintainability, visual refinement, and incomplete or inconsistent functionality.

sections.heading: Technology and outcome
paragraph: Butta uses React, TypeScript, Vite, React Router DOM, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, and OGL for its WebGL background.
The project demonstrates a component-driven shop experience with API-powered products, typed cart state, search, sorting, discounts, ratings, and responsive layouts.

article.description: Butta is a JavaScript framework project created to demonstrate component-driven interfaces, structured application code, and practical frontend problem solving.
improvementReason: Redesigned the hero and layout with marquee text, responsive spacing, and a smooth bottom fade.
Replaced the original orange buttons with a liquid-glass visual style and improved contrast across cards, fields, cart information, and notifications.
Improved mobile navigation, focus states, product tags, ratings, search, and sale filtering.
Lazy-loaded the WebGL background, consolidated discount logic, fixed a checkout update loop, corrected local-storage behavior, and added documentation.
article.process: The project focused on translating requirements into reusable components, organizing the interface, and refining the experience through testing and iteration.

sections.heading: Project overview
paragraph: Barter is a modern, responsive auction house platform built as part of the Semester Project 2 assignment at NOROFF. The platform allows users to create listings, place bids, manage their profiles, and participate in auctions using a credit-based system.
The project was later refined for the POR2 portfolio assignment, with a focus on visual polish, responsive behavior, accessibility, and clearer user feedback.

sections.heading: Development process
paragraph: Barter was created for the NOROFF Semester Project 2 assignment. The brief required a student-only auction application integrated with the Noroff Auction House API, including listings, profiles, bidding, credits, and authentication.
The project was later refined for Portfolio 2 with a focus on lecturer feedback, maintainability, responsive behavior, accessibility, dark mode, and visual presentation.

image.caption: The Barter bidding interface and listing cards.

sections.heading: Technology and outcome
paragraph: Barter uses Vanilla JavaScript with ES6 modules, HTML, Tailwind CSS, Flowbite and Lucide icons, and the Noroff v2 Auction House API.
The result is a responsive auction experience with authentication, listing management, bidding, profile features, theme support, and improved mobile controls.

article.description: Barter is a semester project for an online auction house. The experience is designed to make browsing listings, understanding item information, and taking action feel clear and accessible.
improvementReason: Added persistent light/dark mode with a header toggle and theme-aware logos.
Improved mobile controls, login icons, spacing, form controls, labels, footer styling, profile avatars, and hover states.
Added Cabinet Grotesk typography to Home and Listings headings, clearer copy, highest-bid information, auction subheadings, and a signup marquee.
Added password visibility controls, confirm-password validation, improved bid indicators, and a shared safe API response parser.
article.process: The project combined interface planning, responsive implementation, content hierarchy, and iterative refinement of the core auction flows.

article.title: Sløvstuggu-GCG
article.subheading: A community marketplace for Gundam Card Game collectors in Norway

image.alt: A modern and high-tech landing page
image.caption: A modern and responsive interface for trading Gundam GCG cards

sections.heading: A home for Gundam Card Game collectors
paragraph: SLØVSTUGGU TCG is a work-in-progress community platform for players and collectors of the Gundam Card Game in Norway.
The website is being developed to make it easier to discover cards, manage collections, and connect with other enthusiasts.

sections.heading: Trading through Discord
paragraph: Trades and sales are intended to take place through the Gundam Card Game Norway Discord community.
The website helps members find cards and sellers, while Discord remains the place to discuss prices, shipping, payment, and trade details.

sections.heading: Explore the marketplace
sections.paragraph: The marketplace gives users an overview of cards available from other collectors. Visitors can browse card details, compare listings, view prices, and contact sellers through Discord.

sections.heading: Collections and wishlists
sections.paragraph: Planned features include personal digital collections and wishlists. Members will be able to keep track of cards they own, save cards they are looking for, and eventually receive notifications when wanted cards become available.

image.caption: A preview of the planned user-focused collection experience.

sections.heading: Work in progress and future plans
sections.paragraph: The website is still under development. User signup and registration have not yet been implemented, so access is currently limited while the platform is being built and tested.

article.description: SLØVSTUGGU TCG is a Norwegian-focused community marketplace for Gundam Card Game collectors and players.
improvementReason: Future plans include improved collection management, price tracking, Discord notifications, user profiles, trader ratings, expanded search tools, and support for additional card games and communities.
article.process: The platform is being developed around the existing Gundam Card Game Norway Discord community, with the website acting as a structured discovery and marketplace layer.
